headline: Free up 10GB of Gmail space in 5 minutes without deleting important emails
summary: Discover how to reclaim gigabytes of storage by targeting large attachments and old files, all without sacrificing essential emails.
details: Tired of Gmail's storage limits? One writer found a way to free up a massive 10GB of space in just five minutes, and the best part is, no important emails had to be deleted.
The key lies in identifying and bulk-deleting large attachments. While individual emails are small, hundreds of 2MB attachments can quickly eat up your 15GB free storage.

Using the Google One app or Gmail's advanced search operators like 'larger:10M has:attachment', you can quickly find and remove these space-hogging files. The mobile app even treats attachment size as searchable metadata.

Beyond attachments, Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides created or edited after June 1, 2021, now count towards your storage quota. Regularly clearing out old drafts or unneeded files in these apps can also help.

The writer also highlights Gmail's new one-click unsubscribe button and the 'Manage Subscriptions' feature, which streamline the process of opting out of unwanted email newsletters, further decluttering your inbox.
